bhadrapīṭha
(‘the auspicious pedestal’)
------------------------------------------
A पीठ is a pedestal for an icon. Out of the four varieties mentioned in iconographical works, भद्रपीठ is one, the other three being पद्मपीठ, vedikā and parimaṇḍala.
If the height of the pedestal is sixteen units accommodated in eight parts, then, it is called ‘bhadrapīṭha’. The parts reckoned from the bottom to the top as also their measurements are as follows:
(1) upāna 1 unit
(2) jagatī 4 units
(3) kumuda 3 units
(4) kampa 1 unit
(5) kaṇṭha 3 units
(6) kampa 1 unit
(7) paṭṭikā 2 units
(8) ghṛtavāri 1 unit

See also PĪṬHA.

Bhadra-kālī
(‘the Auspicious Kālī’)
------------------------------------------
Worship of God as मोथेर् has been in vogue in India since the most ancient times. Out of the several aspects of the मोथेर् Goddess that are still worshipped, an overwhelming majority are forms of पार्वती or शक्ति, the consort of शिव. Bhadrakālī is one of them.
Since ‘bhadra’ means auspiciousness, Bhadrakālī is a pleasing deity with a charming appearance. She is depicted as seated on a chariot drawn by four lions. She has eighteen hands in which she carries things such as rosary, trident, sword, shield, bow and arrow, conch, discus, sacrificial ladles, holy water-pot, spear and so on. One of the hands is raised in the gesture of benediction.
The girl-child of यशोदा which was brought to the prison by Vasudeva, the ड़थेर् of कृष्ण, after exchanging it with baby कृष्ण, and which कṁस tried to kill, was also Bhadrakālī. She is an aspect of दुर्गा.
The Kālikāpurāṇa (ch. 59) however describes Bhadrakālī as an aspect of दुर्गा, and as an exceedingly terrible deity. The demon महिषासुर saw her in dream and was stricken with mortal fear. He worshipped her and got the boon to be killed directly by her. She also granted an additional boon that he too would be worshipped in future along with her.
According to another account भद्र-काली was the female companion of Vīra-bhadra, who had been created by शिव out of a hair from his matted locks to destroy दक्ष’s sacrifice.

Bhadrācalam
(‘mountain of Bhadra’)
------------------------------------------
Bhadrācalam—also known as Bhadra-giri—is considered as one of the 25 important places of पिल्ग्रिमगे associated with Śrī राम. It is situated in the Khammam district of Andhra Pradesh. It is 50 kms. (31 miles) from Kothagudem, the place famous for the coal mines of Singareni.
भद्राचलम्">Śrī Ramā Temple at BhadrācalamThe sanctum of the temple has all the three images, of Śrī राम, सीता and लक्ष्मण. According to the स्थलपुराण (local mythological accounts), the three appeared before the sage Bhadra (personification of the mountain Bhadragiri, consi-dered as the son of Meruparvata or mountain मेरु and Menakā) and transformed themselves into stone images at his request, to stay there permanently. An anthill grew over the images and they were hidden from the human gaze for centuries.
The presence there of the images was revealed accidentally or by divine dispensation to one Pokala Dammakka, a childless widow who had adopted a boy named राम. She retrieved the images and preserved them, offering a simple worship. One day in a dream she saw the sage Bhadra who instructed her to keep up her devoted worship until such a time when a great devotee of Śrī राम will come and construct a temple for the images. Later, when Kañcarla Gopanna (A.

-1687) who was the tax-collector of the Muslim ruler Tanisha visited the place, she revealed her dream to him. Since he was a great devotee of Śrī राम, he got the temple built. Though he was punished by the ruler for the ‘misuse’ of State funds, Śrī राम came to his rescue in a miraculous way.
Gopanna became a famous composer-musician, now well-known as Bhadrācala रामदास.
The temple was built in the 17th century and was thoroughly renovated during the 1960’s.
Śrī राम-Navamī and वैकुण्ठ एकादशी are the biggest festivals conducted in this temple.
Temples of नरसिṁह and Govinda-rāja as also the रामदास Dhyānamandira are places of importance for the pilgrims.
About 36 kms. (20 miles) away is the Parṇaśālā where Śrī राम and Sīta stayed, before सीता was abducted by रावण, the demon-king. A rivulet, Śītāvāga by name, flows nearby.
Dummaguḍem (16 kms. or 10 miles from भद्राचलम्) where Śrī राम is said to have killed Khara and his army of 14,000 demons, as also Guṇḍala (5 kms. or 3 miles down the river, from Bhadrā-calam) containing hot springs are other places of interest.

bhadrāsana
(‘the auspicious posture,’ ‘the auspicious seat’)
------------------------------------------
Āsanas or योगासनस् are various postures of the body aimed at freeing it from diseases and improving its health, energy and stamina. Out of the 32 āsanas most commonly practised, भद्रासन is one. In this posture, one has to sit on one’s knees, allowing the calf-muscles touch the thighs. Hands should be taken to the back and catch hold of the toes with the fingers. This should be followed by Jālandhara-बन्ध, wherein the gaze is fixed on the tip on the nose.
In another variety, the hands have to cross each other. The right hand should hold the left toe and the left, the right toe.
This आसन is said to cure the stiffness of bones and rigidity of ligaments.
In iconographical works, it represents a golden throne with cushions.
See also JĀLANDHARA-BANDHA and YOGĀSANAS.
